title: Align the shelf-label units
hook: €0.80 per 100g or €7 per kg: which label is lower?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Convert prices quoted per 100g and per kilogram to a common unit.

misconception: The smaller number on a price label is always cheaper.
objective: Convert prices quoted per 100g and per kilogram to a common unit.

claims.text: A is €0.80 per 100g. B is €7 per kg. Scaled model; fictional prices; 1kg=1000g.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Kg-price=7€, A=8€/kg and B=7€/kg. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",0.8,10]; B="x"; x denotes Kg-price. At x=7, A=8, B=7. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: A kilogram contains ten 100g units. Multiply the 100g price by ten before comparing. A smaller printed price can describe a smaller amount rather than a cheaper product.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",0.8,10]; B="x"; x denotes Kg-price. At x=7, A=8, B=7. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Two fictional shelf labels: €0.65 per 100g and €6 per kg. Which is lower per kilogram? Correct: €6 per kg. A kilogram is ten 100g units, so €0.65 per 100g is €6.50 per kg; the smaller printed number described a smaller amount.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",0.8,10]; B="x"; x denotes Kg-price. At x=7, A=8, B=7. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. claims.text: A unit price expresses cost per stated quantity; comparable unit-price labels use consistent units of measure.
claims.source: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/1181e2025/NIST.SP.1181e2025.html NIST SP 1181-2025, Definitions / Unit Pricing and E-Commerce. Opened 2026-10-13. Dataset prices and package amounts are invented for the arithmetic demonstration.
